newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Business leader blasts religion on birth control.
newsitem.headline: Business leader blasts religion on birth control.

text.p: A Mexican steel magnate representing international big business lashed out during the U.N. Earth Summit on Wednesday against religions that ban birth control.

"In some religions, preventing pregnancy is a sin, and whoever practices birth control, they say, will end up in hell," said Eugenio Clariond Rehes, representing the International Chapter of Commerce.
"What in the world are they talking about?" he asked.

Without mentioning Roman Catholicism directly, he added: "There is no worst condemnation than how they are living now -- lacking the most essential human needs, living in poverty, pollution and hunger, living with illness and in ignorance. They are already in hell. How much worse can they be?"
Clariond Reyes said most population growth occurred in poor countries where education was at a premium.
He said that in Mexico 60 percent of the population was below the age of 23. "We already have difficulties meeting this sector's educational needs, which are essential for a better future."
He said that that environmental concerns have become one of the highest corporate priorities but a strategy was still needed to involve smaller corporations, particularly in developing countries.
Clariond Reyes, who heads the Mexican Council of Business Men, comprising 34 wealthy chief executives, is chairman of the steel company Grupo Imsa.
